title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
abstract: arXiv:2611.03424v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Research taste, the judgment of what to read, which problems to pursue, and which methods to try, increasingly shapes the work of AI scientists, yet it remains far less understood than their ability to execute research. We introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that scores an LLM by how closely the research proposals it writes from a literature snapshot frozen at 2025 match the work the same communities published in 2026. Our experiments span six contemporary language models and four research areas from established to emerging fields, covering more than 90{,}000 proposals in total. LLM agents fall well short of human communities in both the literature they cite and the ideas they state, reaching about 26\% of the human level on citation matching and only 18\% on idea matching. Their populations can cite as diversely as a community and take up its tasks and methods, yet rarely arrive at the concrete approaches and research plans it pursues. Nei

translated_title: IdeaTaste：大语言模型是否拥有与人类研究者相同的研究品味？
translated_abstract: 研究品味，即对阅读什么文献、追求哪些问题、尝试哪些方法的判断力，正日益塑造着AI科学家的工作，但相比其执行研究的能力，这一能力却远未被充分理解。我们提出了IdeaTaste，这是一个基准测试，通过衡量大语言模型基于2025年冻结的文献快照所撰写的研究提案，与相同研究社区在2026年实际发表工作的匹配程度来为其评分。我们的实验涵盖六个当代语言模型和四个研究领域（从成熟领域到新兴领域），共计超过90,000份提案。实验表明，LLM智能体在所引用的文献和所陈述的想法方面都远不及人类社区：在引用匹配上仅达到人类水平的约26%，在想法匹配上仅达到18%。LLM群体的引用多样性可以达到社区水平，也能采纳社区的任务和方法，但很少能提出该社区所追求的具体研究方法和研究计划。
tldr: IdeaTaste基准通过将LLM基于2025年文献快照撰写的研究提案与人类社区2026年的实际发表工作进行匹配评分，发现LLM在引用匹配和想法匹配上仅达到人类水平的约26%和18%，揭示了LLM尚不具备人类研究者的研究品味。
